items.followUp: Which HTML tag is used to insert a line break?

rubric.why: A definition of sabotage must indicate deliberate harmful action.
rubric.description: Defines sabotage as intentional damage to or disruption of a system.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear definition involving deliberate damage or disruption of computer systems, networks, or data.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate damage, destruction, or disruption of a computer system, network, or its data.

items.followUp: What is meant by unauthorized access to a computer system?

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer system or network.

items.followUp: Name the five components of a data communication system and briefly describe each.

rubric.why: The definition should describe the exchange or transmission of data between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that data is exchanged or transmitted between devices.

rubric.why: Sender and receiver are the communicating endpoints.
rubric.description: Identifies the sender and receiver as components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both endpoints and their roles.

rubric.why: The message is the data being sent, and the medium carries it.
rubric.description: Identifies the message and transmission medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the data/message and the communication medium.

rubric.why: Protocols are the rules that govern data communication.
rubric.description: Identifies the communication protocol and its role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying protocols as the rules used for communication.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
The sender is the device that sends the data, and the receiver is the device that receives it.
The message is the data being communicated; the medium is the path through which it travels.
A protocol is the set of rules that controls how devices communicate.

items.followUp: What is a malicious link? Give two warning signs that an e-mail containing one may be phishing.

rubric.why: Phishing is a deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information, often through a fraudulent e-mail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a deceptive e-mail or message intended to steal sensitive information.

rubric.why: Phishing e-mails commonly pretend to come from a trusted organization or person.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: impersonation or a misleading trusted appearance.

rubric.why: Phishing messages often pressure recipients to act quickly.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: urgency or a threatening demand.

rubric.why: Phishing messages often seek sensitive details or direct users to harmful links or attachments.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: requests sensitive information or includes a suspicious link or attachment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these features.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is an attempt to trick a person into revealing sensitive information by using a deceptive e-mail or message.
A phishing e-mail may pretend to come from a trusted person or organization.
It may create urgency or threaten consequences to make the recipient act quickly.
It may ask for passwords or other personal information, or contain a suspicious link or attachment.

items.followUp: Write the four steps used to solve a problem using the problem-solving method.

rubric.why: The first step is to understand or define what needs to be solved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid first step.

rubric.why: The remaining steps involve planning or designing a solution, carrying it out, and checking it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer gives the three remaining steps in a valid problem-solving sequence.

modelAnswer: Devise a plan or design a solution.
Carry out the plan or implement the solution.
